title: Behind the new gateway Ingress, every anonymous client shares one rate-limit bucket (the ingress-nginx pod IP)
evidence: services/gateway/internal/proxy/gateway.go:192-210: rateKey uses "ip:"+clientIP(r) and clientIP = r.RemoteAddr (comment: 'dat sau ingress/LB thi phai cau hinh proxy tin cay truoc khi doi o day'). Auth routes (/api/v1/auth/, RateAuth 1 rps burst 10) are ALWAYS keyed by IP, even when logged in (gateway.go:193). AC-23 puts api.eventflow.localtest.me (and staging, runbook 4.1) behind ingress-nginx, so RemoteAddr is the controller pod IP for all users: login/register for the whole user base is limited to ~1 rps per gateway replica, anonymous Public routes share 10 rps. identity also logs X-Forwarded-For set by gateway = controller IP. Not listed in runbook section 9 or spec section 9.
fix: Record as a staging blocker/known limit in runbook section 9 and spec section 9 (code change is out of scope here), and open a debt item: gateway trusts X-Forwarded-For only from a configured CIDR (ingress-nginx namespace pod CIDR) with ingress-nginx use-forwarded-headers/compute-full-forwarded-for and Service externalTrafficPolicy: Local. Interim: document RATE_AUTH/RATE_DEFAULT overrides for staging.

title: AC-32 fail-closed check is bypassed by a duplicate env name (checker reads the first entry, Kubernetes uses the last)
evidence: present() returns the FIRST env item with the name; kubelet applies env in order so the LAST duplicate wins. The overlays add env with JSON-patch 'op: add path: .../env/-', exactly the idiom that appends a duplicate. Repro: take the staging render JSON, append {name: GEMINI_MOCK, value: '1'} to ai-worker and {name: PAYMENT_ENABLED_PROVIDERS, value: sandbox} to payment, run `python -I deploy/k8s/policy/check_policy.py --overlay staging --input dup.json` -> 'policy: OK (57 objects, overlay=staging)'. Effective config would be mock Gemini and the in-process sandbox provider in staging. kubeconform does not flag duplicate env names either.
fix: Reject duplicate env names per container (new sub-check, via a TCR with one bad fixture), or at minimum make _env_value/present evaluate the last occurrence. Add a bad fixture 'AC-32--duplicate-env-overrides'.

title: C4.4 creates namespace eventflow for real on whatever cluster the current context points at
evidence: The Job delete is correctly guarded by ^(docker-desktop|kind-.+)$, but `kubectl create namespace eventflow` (line 247) and the server dry-run of overlays/local (dev-infra + dev Secret payloads) run on ANY reachable context, e.g. a staging/prod context. The namespace is created without PSA labels (restricted is only added by a later real apply). Pre-existing behaviour (old code applied 00-namespace.yaml), but now easy to hit when an operator's context points at staging.
fix: Apply the same context guard to the namespace creation (and ideally to the whole C4.4 dry-run); on a non-local context log that C4.4 was skipped, or dry-run overlays/staging instead.

title: Monitoring namespaces may reach backend API ports, not just /metrics
evidence: Per spec 6.2, allow-{identity,event,waitingroom,ticketing,payment,ai-worker} admit any pod in a namespace labelled eventflow.io/monitoring=true on the API port. NetworkPolicy cannot restrict path, so such a pod can send forged X-Identity-Id to backends (F9) and POST /admin/mode/{mode} on ai-worker (services/ai-worker/app/main.py:185, blocked only at the gateway). The label is settable by anyone who can patch namespaces. Matches the approved matrix, so not a defect, but the residual risk is not written down.
fix: Add to runbook section 8: only label namespaces that run Prometheus, and treat the label as privileged. Debt item: serve metrics on a separate port (as gateway/controller/worker do) and narrow the monitoring rule to it.

title: Spec mitigation 'secret scan in full gate' / D4 'secret scanning baseline must allow secrets.dev.env' has no implementation
evidence: No gitleaks/trufflehog/detect-secrets config or step in .github/ or gates.sh (grep -ri gitleaks|trufflehog|detect-secrets .github -> nothing). Only AC-16/AC-17 guard credentials, and AC-17 only sees rendered env literals/ConfigMaps.
fix: Either correct the spec/runbook (no secret scanner exists; AC-16/17 are the only guard) or add a pinned secret scan with an allowlist for overlays/local/secrets.dev.env and testdata.

title: A workload labelled eventflow.io/tier=dev-infra escapes app rules and is not rejected in the staging render
evidence: dev_infra is decided only by the label; dev-infra skips noRunAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem, tmpEmptyDir, and may use AC-6/10/11/20 exemptions. No rule fails a dev-infra object in overlay=staging (spec D6: dev-infra is local only). A new non-process Deployment in staging could self-label dev-infra and carry an arbitrary upstream image. AC-1 only protects the 11 named processes.
fix: Via TCR: fail any object with eventflow.io/tier=dev-infra when --overlay staging (e.g. under AC-21 or AC-1) and add one bad staging fixture.

title: AC-17 does not inspect container command/args or key=value DSNs
evidence: check_ac17 only looks at env[].value and ConfigMap data. A credential in args (e.g. goose DSN 'host=... password=...' as in compose's migrate service) or a libpq key=value DSN in an env literal not named *PASSWORD* passes; CRED_URL_RE only matches URL userinfo.
fix: Extend AC-17 to command/args and to a '(?i)\bpassword=' pattern; add one fixture (TCR).

title: Runbook staging section does not cover TLS on the Ingresses
evidence: Staging values are https (CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, VNPAY/MOMO return URLs, MOMO_NOTIFY_URL=https://api.staging...), but base Ingresses have no tls section and runbook 4.1 only says to patch hosts. MoMo IPN and browsers will hit https; without a tls block/cert the staging apply cannot serve these URLs.
fix: Add to runbook 4.1 a temporary-overlay patch adding spec.tls (secretName or cert-manager annotation) for both Ingresses, and list it as a precondition.

title: TOOLS=docker mode fails with the default render dir
evidence: Default RENDER_DIR is $TMP/render (mktemp -d, outside the repo). relrender() returns the host path when RENDER_DIR is not under ROOT, but kubeconform/yq containers only mount ROOT at /w, so they cannot read the render. Default TOOLS=go and CI are unaffected; contract section 6 lists docker as an optional mode.
fix: In docker mode default RENDER_DIR to a dir under the repo (gitignored) or mount RENDER_DIR into the containers.

title: TCR-WP5 applied to frozen fixtures without a recorded human approval
evidence: tcr-applied.md says TCR-WP5 was applied by WP6; test-change-request-wp5.md line 3 still reads 'Status: open, optional ... Needs human approval like any test change after freeze'. The change only adds a fixture (strengthens tests), but the v3 process requires the approval to be recorded.
fix: Record the human approval (date, who) in tcr-applied.md and update the request status, or revert the fixture.

title: Dev-infra image tags are floating minor/patch tags
evidence: postgres:16-alpine, redis:7-alpine (redis.yaml:47), rabbitmq:3.13-management-alpine (rabbitmq.yaml:55), axllent/mailpit:v1.21 (mailpit.yaml:46) satisfy AC-21 but move under the same tag; the uids (70, 999:1000, 100:101, 1000) hard-coded in runAsUser were read from one specific build and could change. pgbouncer is pinned to v1.25.2-p0.
fix: Pin to full patch versions (e.g. postgres:16.x-alpine3.y) or @sha256 digests; local-only, so low priority.

title: C4.4 renders with kubectl's built-in kustomize, not the pinned v5.7.1 validated by validate.sh/CI
evidence: `kubectl apply --dry-run=server -k overlays/local` uses whatever kustomize the local kubectl bundles (kubectl 1.30 ships kustomize v5.0.x); runbook 3.2 and validate.sh use the pinned binary. The dry-run may check a different render than the one the policy approved.
fix: When ~/.cache/eventflow-k8s/bin/kustomize-<pin> exists, pipe its build into `kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f -` (filtering the migrate Job when needed); otherwise keep -k and log the kustomize version used.

title: DEV ONLY header block is duplicated
evidence: Lines 1-4 and 6-9 are the same comment block.

title: AC-30 and AC-31 are NOT VERIFIED; merge needs the explicit human sign-off the spec requires
evidence: runbook section 9: overlays/local never applied (migrate Job, readiness, PDB, NetworkPolicy), staging server dry-run not run, image builds/uids not run. Several runtime assumptions are only reasoned, not observed (postgres/rabbitmq fsGroup on hostpath, pgbouncer/rabbitmq as non-root uid, distroless/python under readOnlyRootFilesystem).
fix: Record the human sign-off for NOT VERIFIED explicitly before merge, or run section 3 on Docker Desktop/kind and attach the evidence.
